mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (measured as the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS) signals monetary tightening, which increases discount rates for equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.1% in the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% (measured as the current UNRATE value) signals an impending labor market slowdown, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and labor market strength (PAYEMS) signals a weakening economy, as reduced consumer demand and lower employment growth suppress corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when either RSAFS or PAYEMS shows a decline in isolation (i.e., one series declines but the other does not), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% and rising for three consecutive months signals aggressive rate hikes, which compress equity valuations and cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0 and rising for 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (measured as the 1-month change in UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE declines by at least 0.1 percentage points in the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1150 thousand units (measured as the current HOUST value) signals weakness in the residential construction sector, which reduces consumer wealth and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST falls below 1150.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a supply-side economic slowdown, which reduces corporate output and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when either INDPRO or GDPC1 shows a decline in isolation (i.e., one series declines but the other does not), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105.0 (measured as the current INDPRO value) signals a contraction in manufacturing and services output, which reduces corporate earnings growth and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO falls below 105.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
